title: Kafka: One Topic, Two Totally Different Behaviors
description:
A single Kafka topic can behave like a work queue or a broadcast to every subscriber -- and the switch isn't a special queue type, it's the consumer's group ID. We break down the producer key, the consumer group config, and how Kafka quietly supports both point-to-point and pub/sub messaging on the exact same topic.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/06-messaging-event-driven/

#Shorts

beats.narration: One Kafka topic. Same messages. But whether every service gets its own copy, or they split the work between them, comes down to a single config value.

display.heading: Pub/Sub or Queue?
display.subheading: Kafka picks based on ONE setting

beats.narration: The producer sends every order event keyed by the order ID -- that key guarantees all events for that order land in the same partition, in order.
The consumer sets a group ID. Two consumers in the same group split the topic between them -- a work queue. Give one a different group ID, and it gets a full copy of every message -- pub/sub.
That's the whole trick: Kafka doesn't have separate queue and topic types like RabbitMQ does -- the consumer group ID is the switch.

display.heading: Point-to-point vs Pub/Sub
display.subheading: Same group ID = split work. Different group ID = full broadcast.
